clue.text: There's nothing to indicate this is a billet-doux

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis, so it stands for nothing
to note something is to point it out or indicate it

explanation.surface: Someone insists there is no sign at all that this letter is a romantic one.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet-doux is French for a sweet little letter, a written message of affection.

clue.text: The best mounted notice

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the word is written upwards, so read from the bottom

parts.note: the tops is a colloquial term for the very best

explanation.surface: A notice board displays the finest notice of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns TOPS upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to see or detect it, a common synonym.

clue.text: Their first mistake was creating fear

indicators.note: first signals that only the opening letter of the word Their is used

parts.note: an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A group's very first blunder frightened everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is extreme fear, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A bloomer Poles had to make!

indicators.note: the letters given are used to make, or construct, a new word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some Polish people made a blunder that they had to own up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a gaffe but here it is literally a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-like plant with flowers, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Standard for a clown

definitions.meaning: a criterion or benchmark against which something is tested
the jester in Shakespeare's comedy As You Like It

explanation.definitionFit: A touchstone was a stone used to test gold, hence any standard; it is also the name of a Shakespearean jester.

clue.text: A measure that's of assistance to a Highlander

parts.note: a gill is a small liquid measure, a quarter of a pint
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A drink of whisky is just what a Scotsman needs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase: a GILLIE is a Scottish attendant, someone who assists a Highland sportsman or chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A gillie is a hunting or fishing attendant in the Scottish Highlands, a helper to the locals.

clue.text: Be in contention about money and that's all!

indicators.note: about means the first word is placed around the second

parts.note: to be in contention is to compete
L is the abbreviation for pound, a unit of money

explanation.surface: A rival fighting over cash concludes that is the whole matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts COMPETE around L, the pound sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete means entire or whole, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Get engaged

parts.note: reads like becoming betrothed, but means getting tangled up or caught in a net

explanation.definitionFit: To be caught in a mesh or net is to be entangled, or engaged in the mechanical sense.

clue.text: Impassive holy man requiring no covering

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man
O is zero or nothing, so no
a lid is a covering for a container

explanation.surface: An unmoved saint needs no head covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid means showing little emotion, the same as unmoved.

clue.text: The others don't work

explanation.definitionFit: Rest as a noun is the remainder; as a verb it is to relax and be idle.

clue.text: Sheep hobble and tumble down

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
to hobble an animal is to fetter or shackle its legs

explanation.surface: A tethered sheep stumbles and falls over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumble down' looks like a verb but is the adjective tumbledown, meaning dilapidated.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbledown building is falling to pieces, a synonym for dilapidated.

clue.text: An idler of real potential

indicators.note: potential means something possible but not yet formed, so the letters can still be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A lazy person with true promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer is someone who idles around, a lazy person.

clue.text: Flaming clear-out!

parts.note: sounds like an exasperated cry about a purge, but describes how to get clear of a burning building

explanation.definitionFit: A fire escape is an exit stair used to get out when a building is burning.

clue.text: Take avoiding action, as crabby creatures always do

definitions.meaning: crabs walk sideways, stepping to the side

explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep is to dodge by moving aside; crabs literally step sideways.

clue.text: Royalty go on travelling

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen and so for royalty
to rant is to go on at length loudly

explanation.surface: The monarch keeps talking on and on while on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant in its old sense means wandering, as in a knight errant who roams in search of adventure.

clue.text: Want fish, which is provoking

parts.note: to want is to need
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Craving fish, which annoys others.
explanation.definitionFit: Needling means annoying or goading someone, a synonym for provoking.

clue.text: A boorish guy about fifty going at full speed

indicators.note: about means the first word is wrapped around the second

parts.note: a lout is an uncouth, boorish man
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A rough fellow around fifty years old racing along as fast as he can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts LOUT around L, giving LLOUT after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: All-out means with maximum effort, flat out.

clue.text: A model suit

definitions.meaning: an example that others follow or are judged by
a lawsuit, a case brought in court

explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a lawsuit whose outcome sets a precedent and so serves as an example.

clue.text: A man about to cut a woman

indicators.note: cut means these letters slice into the middle of another word

parts.note: her is a pronoun standing for a woman
C is the abbreviation of circa, meaning about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fellow is on the point of stabbing a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like violence but is the container signal; 'A man' is the definition, a Trojan hero's name rather than any fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector is a man's name, best known as the Trojan hero.

clue.text: Swiss twits holding archdeacon back

indicators.note: holding means the first word contains the second

parts.note: geese are silly people, a colloquial word for fools

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: Foolish Swiss people restraining a senior cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twits' as GEESE is an old colloquial insult; 'back' reverses the archdeacon's title and 'holding' sets it inside. Ven is short for Venerable, the formal style of an archdeacon.
explanation.definitionFit: Genevese describes something or someone from Geneva, a Swiss city.

clue.text: Jubilant send-up of French misrepresentation

indicators.note: in a down clue, a send-up means the letters go upwards, so they read backwards

parts.note: de is French for of
a tale is a fib or misleading story

explanation.surface: A gleeful parody of a lie from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'send-up' sounds like a parody but turns DETALE upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated means overjoyed, a synonym for jubilant.

clue.text: In principle a secretary should have charm

indicators.note: In signals the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Ideally, a personal assistant ought to be charming.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across principLE A SEcretary.
explanation.definitionFit: To please is to delight or charm someone.

clue.text: Left a person lacking experience in the doorway

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a novice standing at the entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is the nautical word for the left-hand side; L plates mark learner drivers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A portal is a grand doorway or entrance.

clue.text: Needing settlement, call a court assessor

indicators.note: the letters are unsettled, waiting to be arranged into order

explanation.surface: Seeking to resolve a dispute, summon a court official.
explanation.definitionFit: A calculator works out or assesses figures, so it is something that assesses.

clue.text: Career people

definitions.meaning: to career is to rush along at speed

explanation.definitionFit: To race is to rush headlong; a race is also a group of people sharing descent.

clue.text: Using more foreign capital

indicators.note: foreign suggests something made strange or altered, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: Spending more on a city abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome is the capital city of Italy.

clue.text: No peer is disposed to start afresh

indicators.note: disposed here means arranged or set out, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: No nobleman is inclined to begin again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reopen is to begin again after a closure.

clue.text: The most backward raise the biggest families

parts.note: to rear children is to raise them
most means the greatest amount, the biggest

explanation.surface: A jibe that the least advanced people bring up the largest broods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'families' completes the surface: those who rear families most.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearmost means furthest at the back, the last of all.
